item.title: Imaging hot-electron Thomson cooling beyond the Boltzmann–Onsager framework
item.author: Xinrong ZuoGuokang ZhangZhenghua An
item.content:encoded:
Classical Thomson cooling is inefficient. Now non-equilibrium energy dissipation with a breakdown of the Boltzmann–Onsager limit is demonstrated by imaging hot electrons in HgTe and HgCdTe quantum wells.

Xinrong ZuoGuokang ZhangZhenghua An

Nature Physics

item.title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
item.author: Simon RoggorsThomas UndenIlai Schwartz
item.content:encoded:
A triplet carbene molecule in a tailored crystal provides a stable single-molecule spin–photon interface with millisecond coherence, advancing chemically engineered molecular qubits for quantum networking.

Simon RoggorsThomas UndenIlai Schwartz

Nature

item.title: Subcycle videography of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene
item.author: V. EggersG. InzaniU. Höfer
item.content:encoded:
An experimental concept enabling attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone is demonstrated and used to visualize the lightwave-driven electron motion of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene.

V. EggersG. InzaniU. Höfer

Nature

item.title: Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal
item.author: Jianmin HuangQitang FanBing Wang
item.content:encoded:
Planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons are synthesized by laterally fusing polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains, suggesting a possible route towards carbon quantum wires.

Jianmin HuangQitang FanBing Wang

Nature

item.title: Order in a quantum chaotic sea
item.author: Shiyu Wang
item.content:encoded:
Experiments with a superconducting quantum processor revealed an island of regular motion within otherwise chaotic quantum many-body dynamics and used feedback to steer the dynamics towards it.

Shiyu Wang

Nature Physics

item.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
item.author: Yi LiQingyuan MeiJiangfeng Du
item.content:encoded:
Conventional quantum error correction requires repeated measurements and real-time feedback, which are technically complex. An autonomous implementation that eliminates these while beating the break-even point is demonstrated in a trapped-ion system.

Yi LiQingyuan MeiJiangfeng Du

Nature Physics

item.title: Particle collisions on a quantum computer
item.author: Torsten V. Zache
item.content:encoded:
Elementary particle physics rests on the discovery of particles produced in high-energy collider experiments. Now, a model collision above the threshold for particle production has been simulated on a quantum computer.

Torsten V. Zache

Nature Physics

item.title: Elusive snow leopards and evasive particles: Books in brief
item.author: Andrew Robinson
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

Andrew Robinson

Nature

item.title: Daily briefing: What we know about Shamonda virus
item.author: Flora Graham
item.content:encoded:
The death of an immunocompromised man in France has been attributed to a newly discovered virus. Plus, good news about a cancer vaccine for melanoma and ponder whether the way we draw molecules is a lie.

Flora Graham

Nature

item.title: Teleportation transition of surface codes on a superconducting quantum processor
item.author: Yiren ZouHong-Kuan XiaH. Wang
item.content:encoded:
Quantum teleportation is often discussed for individual quantum systems, but fault-tolerant quantum computers will encode information in multiqubit states. Now teleportation of surface code logical states has been demonstrated.

Yiren ZouHong-Kuan XiaH. Wang

Nature Physics

item.title: Narrow-linewidth, piezoelectrically tunable photonic integrated blue laser
item.author: Anat SiddharthAsger B. GardnerTobias J. Kippenberg
item.content:encoded:
Combining a gallium nitride laser diode with a high-Q silicon nitride microresonator results in a low-noise integrated blue laser.

Anat SiddharthAsger B. GardnerTobias J. Kippenberg

Nature Photonics

item.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
item.author: Jinghao DengJiabin XieXiaomeng Liu
item.content:encoded:
The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

Jinghao DengJiabin XieXiaomeng Liu

Nature Physics

item.title: Octupole-driven spin torque switching of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
item.author: Jaimin KangMohammad HamdiPedram Khalili Amiri
item.content:encoded:
All-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions can display both a large TMR and a reciprocal switching effect, octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, enabling nanoscale magnetic memory and potentially room-temperature terahertz spintronic devices.

Jaimin KangMohammad HamdiPedram Khalili Amiri

Nature

item.title: Europe and the rest of the world must come up with an answer to US science strategy
item.author: André Loesekrug-Pietri
item.content:encoded:
André Loesekrug-Pietri

Nature

item.title: Light and mirrors move large quantum computers closer to reality
item.content:encoded:
Scientists improve photon-collecting device that could be used to connect multiple quantum-computing arrays.

Nature

item.title: ‘Fiercely stubborn’: the US scientists continuing their research amid funding cuts
item.author: Virginia Gewin
item.content:encoded:
Researchers working on climate change, diversity, transgender health and international aid have turned to lawsuits, private donors and alternative topics to keep their projects going.

Virginia Gewin

Nature

item.title: Cavity-less Brillouin strong coupling in a solid-state continuous system
item.author: Laura Blázquez MartínezChanglong ZhuBirgit Stiller
item.content:encoded:
Strong coupling between light and matter is typically realized in resonators. Now it is shown that this can happen in a cavity-less waveguide scenario in which the light passes through only once.

Laura Blázquez MartínezChanglong ZhuBirgit Stiller

Nature Physics

item.title: Chaos control with broken symmetries
item.author: Jairo Velasco Jr
item.content:encoded:
By breaking both material and cavity symmetries, waves can be funnelled into robust closed-loop patterns. This dual-symmetry-breaking approach enables the development of a new class of devices for wave-based signal processing and sensing.

Jairo Velasco Jr

Nature Physics

item.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
item.author: Yi-Hsien WuLeon C. CamenzindSeigo Tarucha
item.content:encoded:
Quantum computers require simultaneous control of multiple qubits, which is challenging to achieve in nanoscale semiconductor devices. Now high-fidelity parallel operations have been demonstrated for five silicon spin qubits.

Yi-Hsien WuLeon C. CamenzindSeigo Tarucha

Nature Physics

item.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
item.author: Hyungkun BongChoongjae WonMingu Kang
item.content:encoded:
The experimental realization of intrinsic 2D kagome materials with controllable flat bands has remained challenging. Now a van der Waals kagome material family is shown to host an isolated, gate-tunable flat band down to the monolayer limit.

Hyungkun BongChoongjae WonMingu Kang

Nature Physics

item.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor
item.author: Katerina VaxevaniJon OrtuzarJose Ignacio Pascual
item.content:encoded:
Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

Katerina VaxevaniJon OrtuzarJose Ignacio Pascual

Nature

item.title: Chip-mediated manipulation of photonic quantum skyrmions
item.author: Haoqi ZhaoYichi ZhangLiang Feng
item.content:encoded:
Although photonic quantum skyrmions can be generated as entangled or single-photon states, a means to switch between the two is required for quantum information processing. Now, entangled skyrmions and their manipulation on chip is realized.

Haoqi ZhaoYichi ZhangLiang Feng

Nature Physics

item.title: Order from chaos with adaptive circuits on quantum hardware
item.author: Bibek PokharelHaining PanMaika Takita
item.content:encoded:
Controlling quantum chaos requires using measurement and feedback that survive noise and decoherence. Such control is now achieved in a superconducting quantum processor and reveals a critical transition between quantum and classical dynamics.

Bibek PokharelHaining PanMaika Takita

Nature Physics

item.title: Non-reciprocity in quantum technologies
item.author: Shabir BarzanjehAndré XuerebPeter Rabl
item.content:encoded:
Non-reciprocity in the quantum regime promises unidirectional transport and enhanced sensing, but traditional approaches hinder device integration. This Review highlights magnet-free routes for engineering non-reciprocity in quantum systems.

Shabir BarzanjehAndré XuerebPeter Rabl

Nature Physics

item.title: Experimental observation of critical topology
item.author: Zhi-Kang LinLi-Wei WangJian-Hua Jiang
item.content:encoded:
Experimental evidence indicating that critical gapless topological states can be characterized by the entanglement spectrum and wavefunctions is presented, demonstrating persistence of topology at phase boundaries and extension to higher-dimensional systems.

Zhi-Kang LinLi-Wei WangJian-Hua Jiang

Nature

item.title: Nuclear clocks tick for the first time
item.author: Akio Kawasaki
item.content:encoded:
Ultraprecise clocks that use transitions in atomic nuclei to keep time show promise as a next-generation time standard and for probing fundamental physics.

Akio Kawasaki

Nature

item.title: A nuclear clock synchronized to 229Th
item.author: Beichen HuangGaowei YanShiqian Ding
item.content:encoded:
A nuclear clock synchronized to 229Th establishes laser-addressed nuclei as operational clock references and 229Th:CaF2 as a stable, reproducible solid-state platform for compact nuclear clocks and nuclear quantum sensors.

Beichen HuangGaowei YanShiqian Ding

Nature

item.title: Deterministic and programmable fusion for the scalable generation of photonic graph states
item.author: Yan LiYunfan YangLuming Duan
item.content:encoded:
Graph states entangle many photons in a special structure that is useful for several quantum protocols. Making graph states is often probabilistic and inefficient, but now a deterministic approach using superconducting qubits has been demonstrated.

Yan LiYunfan YangLuming Duan

Nature Physics

item.title: Strong coupling of photon to an electron on helium
item.author: David Pile
item.content:encoded:
David Pile

Nature Photonics

item.title: Self-aligned optical microcomb emerging between octave-separated lasers
item.author: Grégory MoillePradyoth ShandilyaKartik Srinivasan
item.content:encoded:
An architectural inversion shifts integrated optical frequency comb generation from outward broadening around a central pump to filling the spectrum between two octave-separated pumps through a self-aligned parametrically driven cavity soliton, enabling robust self-referencing for future deployable on-chip frequency and time metrology.

Grégory MoillePradyoth ShandilyaKartik Srinivasan

Nature

item.title: Hybrid nanophotonic trap boosts atomic storage and coherence times
item.author: Xiao-Dong He
item.content:encoded:
A hybrid nanophotonic trap that replaces the attractive red-detuned laser field with atom–surface interactions — Casimir–Polder interactions and electrostatic attraction — achieves record-long storage and coherence times for cold atoms coupled to a nanofibre surface.

Xiao-Dong He

Nature Photonics

item.title: Topology from disorder
item.author: Jens HertkornBotond Oreg
item.content:encoded:
Topological phases of matter have long been studied in idealized pure states at absolute zero. Two experiments now show how controlled disorder can give mixed states measurable topological features in quantum simulators.

Jens HertkornBotond Oreg

Nature Physics

item.title: Endlessly self-injection-locked photonic integrated lasers
item.author: Mikael ReichlerSimone BianconiTobias J. Kippenberg
item.content:encoded:
Feedback-phase dispersion in a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit enables a self-injection-locked laser to maintain its locked state at any drive current, resulting in a robust, low-noise, narrow-linewidth integrated laser.

Mikael ReichlerSimone BianconiTobias J. Kippenberg

Nature Photonics

item.title: Aharonov–Bohm interference in a \({\pmb{\mathbb{Z}}}_{\bf{2}}\) lattice gauge theory on a hybrid qubit–oscillator quantum computer
item.author: S. SanerO. BăzăvanA. Bermúdez
item.content:encoded:
Lattice gauge theories are difficult to study using classical computational methods. A dynamic quantum simulation of a lattice gauge theory on a two-site loop has now been demonstrated using a hybrid qubit–oscillator trapped-ion quantum computer.

S. SanerO. BăzăvanA. Bermúdez

Nature Physics

item.title: Quantum field theory dynamics on a spin–phonon quantum computer
item.author: Anton T. ThanSaurabh V. KadamNorbert M. Linke
item.content:encoded:
Many physical systems involve bosons, which are resource-intensive to simulate with a qubit-based quantum computer. Now a hybrid approach that combines qubits and bosons has been used to simulate a quantum field theory of fermions and bosons.

Anton T. ThanSaurabh V. KadamNorbert M. Linke

Nature Physics

item.title: Universal scaling laws for correlated decay of many-body quantum systems
item.author: Wai-Keong MokAvishi PoddarAna Asenjo-Garcia
item.content:encoded:
Decoherence and decay of quantum systems arise from interactions with their environment that can be highly complex. Despite this complexity, bounds on the decay rate are found that are asymptotically tight in several important cases.

Wai-Keong MokAvishi PoddarAna Asenjo-Garcia

Nature Physics

item.title: Quantum field theory dynamics in trapped ions
item.author: Pan-Yu Hou
item.content:encoded:
Computing the real-time dynamics of quantum field theories is intractable for classical devices. Now, the dynamics of two quantum field theories have been observed using hybrid trapped-ion quantum simulators.

Pan-Yu Hou

Nature Physics

item.title: A universal speed limit for collective decay in quantum systems
item.content:encoded:
Quantum systems composed of many particles can decay much faster than the sum of their individual decay rates. Now, a universal speed limit of many-body decay has been revealed, providing bounds on applications that rely on collective emission and a potential constraint on the scalability of quantum technologies.

Nature Physics

item.title: Observation of multiphoton entanglement in resonance fluorescence
item.author: Xiao-Long ZhouJian WangGuang-Can Guo
item.content:encoded:
Multiphoton scattering process is extracted from the resonance fluorescence of a single 87Rb atom. Tripartite entanglement between the photons is verified by a violation of Svetlichny’s inequality. A quantum secret sharing protocol is demonstrated as an application example.

Xiao-Long ZhouJian WangGuang-Can Guo

Nature Photonics

item.title: An information-theoretic proof of the Planckian bound for thermalization
item.author: Paolo AbiusoAlberto RolandiMartí Perarnau-Llobet
item.content:encoded:
Studies of many-body physics have indicated that thermalization processes are bounded by a timescale determined by Planck’s constant. Such a bound has now been proved to apply in general using techniques from quantum information theory.

Paolo AbiusoAlberto RolandiMartí Perarnau-Llobet

Nature Physics

item.title: Strange metal behaviour from underlying bad metallicity
item.author: Simone FratiniIvan DucheminSergio Ciuchi
item.content:encoded:
The origin of the strange metal state is still not known. Now, numerical results suggest that it follows from the quantum statistics of charge carriers, not the temperature dependence of the processes that scatter them.

Simone FratiniIvan DucheminSergio Ciuchi

Nature Physics

item.title: String-breaking dynamics in a quantum simulator
item.author: Arinjoy DeAlessio LeroseChristopher Monroe
item.content:encoded:
The study of string breaking in gauge theories involves the real-time evolution of charges, which is difficult to simulate. Spatiotemporal dynamics of string breaking in a one-dimensional gauge model have now been observed in a trapped-ion platform.

Arinjoy DeAlessio LeroseChristopher Monroe

Nature Physics

item.title: Quantum many-body mixed phase space revealed by hybrid feedback control
item.author: Hang DongJie RenZlatko Papić
item.content:encoded:
Regular and chaotic trajectories can coexist in classical systems, but identifying an equivalent in quantum many-body dynamics is difficult. A feedback protocol on a superconducting processor now reveals and stabilizes such mixed dynamics.

Hang DongJie RenZlatko Papić

Nature Physics

item.title: Lu+ optical frequency references with accuracy verified at the 19th digit
item.author: K. J. ArnoldM. D. K. LeeM. D. Barrett
item.content:encoded:
Two independent 176Lu+ single-ion optical clocks achieve fractional frequency uncertainties near 10−19 and agree at 5.7 × 10−19, advancing precision timekeeping.

K. J. ArnoldM. D. K. LeeM. D. Barrett

Nature

item.title: Daily briefing: Read the text inside a charred, rolled-up scroll
item.author: Flora Graham
item.content:encoded:
Lead detection reveals the ink on burnt sheets of papyrus. Plus, the first radio signals from an exoplanet and how to stay smart in the age of AI.

Flora Graham

Nature

item.title: This super-cold microscope could spur a quantum revolution
item.author: Isabel Gil
item.content:encoded:
The instrument, which operates near absolute zero for hours, will soon ship to a few labs. Researchers are thrilled.

Isabel Gil

Nature

item.title: Road transport of trapped antiprotons
item.author: M. LeonhardtJ. MorgnerC. Smorra
item.content:encoded:
Researchers demonstrate successful road transport of trapped antiprotons, establishing a practical method for moving antimatter to quieter laboratories and substantially improving future tests of matter–antimatter symmetry.

M. LeonhardtJ. MorgnerC. Smorra

Nature

item.title: Weakly interacting spinons and tightly bound triplons in the frustrated quantum spin-Peierls chain
item.author: Pyeongjae ParkBo XiaoAndrew D. Christianson
item.content:encoded:
A combination of one-dimensional magnetic frustration and three-dimensional lattice distortions causes the quantum magnet CuGeO3 to form a dimerized state. Now the authors demonstrate how this interplay affects fractionalized quasiparticles of CuGeO3.

Pyeongjae ParkBo XiaoAndrew D. Christianson

Nature Physics

item.title: An algorithm to generate two-dimensional critical lattice models using competing anyon condensation
item.author: Kaixin JiYu ZhaoLing-Yan Hung
item.content:encoded:
Conformal field theories have a central role in statistical and high-energy theoretical physics. An algorithm to systematically generate critical lattice models described by different conformal field theories has now been identified.

Kaixin JiYu ZhaoLing-Yan Hung

Nature Physics

item.title: Digital quantum simulations of scattering in quantum field theories using W states
item.author: Roland C. FarrellNikita A. ZemlevskiyJohn Preskill
item.content:encoded:
Quantum simulations of field-theory scattering require preparing particles and following their collision dynamics. A digital quantum simulation now reveals the inelastic production of particles in one-dimensional Ising field theory.

Roland C. FarrellNikita A. ZemlevskiyJohn Preskill

Nature Physics
